# Accounts in a currency with no minor unit. A yen is not divided into
# hundredths, so GnuCash gives JPY a smallest unit of 1 and 103 yen is written
# 103, never 103.00.
#
# The amounts here are deliberately odd (103, 1030) rather than round hundreds:
# a figure like 100 survives a wrong two-decimal denominator looking plausible,
# whereas 103 does not.
#
# What this fixture produces: the JPY commodity comes back with fraction 1 and
# the CAD one with 100, and exporting the book writes
#
#   Assets:Bank:JPY 103 JPY
#
# — never 103.00. The KRW account is here for the version-dependent case:
# GnuCash's own table carries the won with hundredths through 5.14 and
# normalises it to 1 from 5.15, so the test reads the won's decimals off the
# commodity instead of asserting a number that changes with the engine.
#
# Verified by tests/unit/services/test_zero_decimal_currency_amounts.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:JPY
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "JPY"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:KRW
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "KRW"

2026-01-10 * "Buy 103 JPY at 0.01 CAD/JPY"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:JPY 103 JPY
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "JPY"
		share_price: "1/100"
		value: "1.03"
	Assets:Bank -1.03 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-1.03"

2026-01-11 * "Buy 1030 KRW at 0.001 CAD/KRW"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:KRW 1030 KRW
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "KRW"
		share_price: "1/1000"
		value: "1.03"
	Assets:Bank -1.03 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-1.03"
